I've farmed this land since I was a young woman. I know what grows here, what the soil likes, what my neighbors plant. Quzhou is wheat and corn country — that's what the land is for, that's what I know how to do, and that's what the grain station will buy. I'm not going to try something new at my age, alone, with my sons in the city.

I have about 10 mu. I'll plant all of it to winter wheat in October, then turn it straight to summer corn after the June harvest. Same rotation I've done for thirty years. My neighbor Lao Zhang uses Jimai 22 wheat — good tillering, the shopkeeper at the supply store says everyone buys it, so I will too. For corn I'll get Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed like always. It's reliable.

Before planting wheat I'll rotary-till the field, throw down compound fertilizer as the base, then topdress with urea when it's jointing in spring. Four waterings for wheat — once before winter sets in to protect the roots, once before jointing, once at heading, one more at grain-fill if it's dry. For summer corn I rotary-till to chop the wheat straw under, plant the seed, base fertilizer down at the same time, topdress again around knee-high. Two irrigations unless the rains come.

I'll spray herbicide on the wheat in early spring when the weeds are small. If I see rust or powdery mildew patches like last year I'll spray again. For corn, just herbicide after emergence. I can't afford to hire help much, so I keep it simple.
